finding.claim: /preview fetches an arbitrary attacker-supplied URL server-side and returns the status and first 500 bytes of the body to the caller, with no validation.

trace.note: preview() is a public Flask route with no auth decorator
url query parameter read with no checks
passed directly to requests.get, which follows redirects by default
status_code and resp.text[:500] returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect check on this path. Attacker can reach localhost, link-local (169.254.169.254), or internal hosts and read up to 500 bytes of the response.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:15-17 has no scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect check. The only host check in the file is app.py:23-25 in /partner, which is a separate route and does not apply to preview().
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter is read unauthenticated at app.py:15 and passed straight to requests.get at app.py:16 (which follows redirects by default), and the status and first 500 bytes of the body are returned at app.py:17, with no closing guard on the /preview path. The trace's line 14 is the `def preview()` line rather than the `@app.route` decorator at line 13, but the claim about it is still accurate.

finding.claim: /partner checks only the initial URL's hostname against an allowlist, then fetches the original URL with redirects enabled, so an allowed host can redirect the server to an internal address.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:26 (allow_redirects defaults to True)

trace.note: partner() is a public Flask route
400 returned if hostname not in ALLOWED_HOSTS (api.partner.example, cdn.partner.example)
requests.get(target) follows 3xx Location headers without re-validation
only status_code returned, so the attacker gets a status oracle rather than the body

finding.guards_checked: Hostname allowlist at app.py:23-25 only. No scheme check, port check, resolved-IP check, DNS pinning, or allow_redirects=False. Redirect bypass is sufficient on its own. A concrete urllib.parse vs urllib3 parser differential was not confirmed and is not claimed.

verdict.guard_found: Only the hostname allowlist at app.py:23-25 (exact set membership on urlparse(target).hostname). It runs once on the initial URL. Nothing re-validates after redirects, and there is no allow_redirects=False on the requests.get at app.py:26.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (app.py:22) is attacker-controlled on an unauthenticated public route, and app.py:26 issues `requests.get(target, timeout=5)` with redirects enabled by default, so an allowlisted host returning a 3xx to an internal address is followed past the check at app.py:24. Impact is limited to a status-code oracle (app.py:27), which is a blind SSRF rather than a full read, but the bypass itself is real.
